prompt: Implement diagonalSums for a square matrix: return a two-element array holding the main diagonal sum (top-left to bottom-right) and the anti-diagonal sum (top-right to bottom-left).
explanation: On the main diagonal the row and column index are equal, so those elements are square[i][i]. On the anti-diagonal the indexes mirror each other: row i pairs with column n - 1 - i. A single loop over i can therefore accumulate both sums at once, and the two totals are packaged into a small result array.
hints: Main diagonal elements have equal row and column index: square[i][i].
For the anti-diagonal, row i uses column n - 1 - i where n is the matrix size.
One loop from 0 to n-1 can add to both running sums; return new int[]{main, anti}.
